---
title: "SCOP function gateway"
description: "A detailed task-oriented gateway to SCOP 0.8.9 runners, plotters, required inputs, output locations, tutorial chapters, and verification commands."
---

This is a learning gateway, not a replacement for the upstream help pages. It maps a research task to a **runner**, a **SCOP-native plotter**, the object contract, and the detailed chapter. For every function, your installed package help is authoritative for exact arguments.

::: {.learning-objectives}
## Learning outcomes

You will learn to:

1. find a SCOP function from the biological task rather than its name;
2. pair computational runners with SCOP plotters;
3. identify the assay, layer, metadata, reduction, backend, or reference required;
4. verify exports and signatures locally before copying tutorial code;
5. record a function call as reproducible evidence.
:::

## 1 · Runtime and local verification

The published runtime contains **314 exports** in SCOP 0.8.9.

```r
library(scop)

packageVersion("scop")
exports <- sort(getNamespaceExports("scop"))
length(exports)

"Harmony_integrate" %in% exports
args(scop::Harmony_integrate)
help("Harmony_integrate", package = "scop")
```

For any copied call:

```r
verify_scop_function <- function(name) {
  stopifnot(name %in% getNamespaceExports("scop"))
  list(
    package_version = as.character(packageVersion("scop")),
    name = name,
    signature = args(getExportedValue("scop", name))
  )
}

verify_scop_function("RunDimsEstimate")
```

If your installed signature differs, adapt to local help and record the version difference. Do not invent a wrapper from a function name.

::: {.input-contract}
**Function-call contract**

Record the input checkpoint, assay/layer, reduction/dimensions, grouping/sample fields, reference/database/model, backend, exact arguments, seed, returned object/result location, plotter, output table, and allowed claim.
:::

## 2 · Input, data access, and object conversion

| Task | SCOP function | Required input | Output / next step | Detailed lesson |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| load named SCOP collection | `LoadScopDataset()` | dataset, collection, cache path | downloaded object/path; audit source and checksum | [inputs](input-formats.qmd) |
| H5 matrix + metadata | `FetchH5()` | data file, metadata file, assay/layer mapping | Seurat object; prove metadata join | [inputs](input-formats.qmd) |
| H5AD conversion | `h5ad_to_srt()` | H5AD plus `zellkonverter` path | Seurat object; validate `.X`/layers/obs/var | [inputs](input-formats.qmd#h5ad-and-loom) |
| Loom conversion | `loom_to_srt()` | Loom plus `loomR`, selected layers | Seurat object; validate spliced/unspliced alignment | [inputs](input-formats.qmd#h5ad-and-loom) |

Low-level 10x H5 and three-file input use Seurat readers first; this is intentional. Enter SCOP after the object contract passes.

## 3 · Cell and spot quality control

| Task | Runner | SCOP plotter | Essential contract | Lesson |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| cell QC metrics/filtering | `RunCellQC()` | `FeatureStatPlot()` | raw counts, species-aware metrics, per-sample review | [single sample](single-cell-case.qmd) |
| doublet database/path | `db_scDblFinder()` | review metadata with SCOP plots | per-library raw counts | [single sample](single-cell-case.qmd) |
| general doublet call | `RunDoubletCalling()` | SCOP QC/dimension plot as appropriate | declared method/rate and raw counts | [single sample](single-cell-case.qmd) |
| contamination correction | `RunDecontX()` | before/after SCOP expression/QC plot | original counts preserved, background/group contract | [single sample](single-cell-case.qmd) |
| spatial spot QC | `RunSpotQC()` | `FeatureStatPlot()` / spatial plot path | Spatial assay, coordinate/image audit | [spatial](spatial-case.qmd) |

Typical signatures:

```r
args(scop::RunDoubletCalling)
args(scop::RunDecontX)
args(scop::RunSpotQC)
```

Successful return does not choose thresholds for you. Save before/after distributions and retained counts by sample.

## 4 · Construction, integration, dimensions, and clustering

| Task | Function | Minimum required fields | Validation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Harmony integration | `Harmony_integrate()` | technical `batch`, assay, normalization contract | pre/post mixing + biology preservation |
| CCA integration | `CCA_integrate()` | shared features/populations | anchors and biological preservation |
| RPCA integration | `RPCA_integrate()` | within-source PCA and related datasets | conservative source correction |
| scVI integration | `scVI_integrate()` | counts, sample field, Python backend | environment/version plus latent diagnostics |
| dimension selection | `RunDimsEstimate()` | valid linear/latent reduction | `DimsEstimatePlot()` and recorded selected dims |
| cluster stability | `ClusterTreePlot()` | multiple resolution metadata columns | transitions across a declared resolution grid |
| cell embedding | `CellDimPlot()` | named reduction, group fields | SCOP-native display with honest labels |

The default course order is `db_scDblFinder()` → `JoinLayers()` → multi-resolution clusters/`ClusterTreePlot()` → SCT + integration when justified → `RunDimsEstimate()`.

Integration method guide:

| Method | Prefer when | Important prerequisite | Stop when |
|---|---|---|---|
| Harmony | shared cell states and explicit technical source | meaningful batch field | biology is erased or condition is confounded |
| CCA | correlated shared structure across datasets | adequate common features | anchors connect unlike populations |
| RPCA | larger related datasets, conservative anchors | within-dataset PCA | shared populations are inadequate |
| scVI | nonlinear latent model and sufficient cells | validated Python environment/counts | backend/model instability or poor preservation |

See [multi-sample](multi-sample.qmd) for executable Harmony arguments and metrics.

## 5 · Markers and annotation

| Task | Runner | Plotter/evidence | Required review | Lesson |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| cluster markers | `FindMarkers()`, `FindAllMarkers()` exported by SCOP | `GroupHeatmap()` and other SCOP expression plots | positive/negative programmes, detection, sample distribution | [annotation](annotation.qmd) |
| CellTypist | `RunCellTypist()` | labels, confidence, SCOP marker/embedding plot | model vocabulary, tissue coverage, unknowns | [annotation](annotation.qmd) |
| SingleR | `RunSingleR()` | prediction/pruning plus marker review | appropriate labelled reference and packages | [annotation](annotation.qmd) |
| RNA/ATAC label transfer | `RunLabelTransfer()` | predicted labels/evaluation | assay class, reference reduction/labels, gene activity | [annotation](annotation.qmd) |

Do not equate classifier confidence with truth. Preserve candidate label, score, final label, uncertainty, and review note as separate fields.

## 6 · Differential expression, enrichment, and composition

| Question | Runner | SCOP plotter | Statistical unit | Lesson |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| show a valid DEG table | external/SCOP result table | `VolcanoPlot()` | inherited from DEG model | [advanced](advanced.qmd) |
| over-representation | `RunEnrichment()` | `EnrichmentPlot()` | inherited from input list/design | [advanced](advanced.qmd) |
| ranked enrichment | `RunGSEA()` | `GSEAPlot()` | inherited from ranked statistic/design | [advanced](advanced.qmd) |
| cell proportion change | `RunPropeller()` | result + `ProportionTestPlot()` path | biological sample | [advanced](advanced.qmd) |
| general proportion test | `RunProportionTest()` | `ProportionTestPlot()` | biological sample when inferential | [advanced](advanced.qmd) |

The plotter cannot repair pseudo-replication. For a condition contrast, construct a sample-level design before running DEG or composition tests.

## 7 · Trajectory and dynamics

| Purpose | Runner | Plotter | Key prerequisites |
|---|---|---|---|
| cluster connectivity/pseudotime | `RunPAGA()` | `PAGAPlot()` | group field, reduction, justified root; optional spliced/unspliced |
| differentiation potential | `RunCytoTRACE()` | `CytoTRACEPlot()` | adequate expressed genes and compatible data |
| lineages | `RunSlingshot()` | returned trajectory/SCOP-supported display | group field, reduction, start/end justification |
| probabilistic trajectory | `RunPalantir()` | `PalantirTrajectoryPlot()` | backend and start cell/state |
| Monocle trajectory | `RunMonocle2()`, `RunMonocle3()` | method-specific result/plot path | compatible counts/object and root |
| velocity extension | `RunSecActVelocity()` | `VelocityPlot()` | aligned spliced/unspliced and backend |

The audited version does **not** export `RunVelocity()`. An ordering or arrow field is not lineage proof; see [advanced analysis](advanced.qmd#trajectory-and-dynamics).

## 8 · Communication, regulation, and metabolism

| Task | Runner | SCOP plotters | Required resources/boundary |
|---|---|---|---|
| cell communication | `RunCellChat()` | `CCCNetworkPlot()`, `CCCHeatmap()`, `CCCStatPlot()` | species DB, group sizes; hypothesis only |
| spatial communication | `RunSpatialCellChat()` | `SpatialCellChatPlot()` | coordinates/technology and spatial distance |
| regulons | `RunSCENIC()` | `SCENICPlot()` | motif rankings/annotations, genome/species, backend |
| SCENIC+ | `RunSCENICPlus()` | corresponding stored results/SCOP display | multiome and additional resources |
| metabolism | `RunMetabolism()` | `MetabolismPlot()` | pathway DB/version, gene coverage, method |

Runner outputs are typically stored in an assay, metadata, or `srt@tools` under a tool name. Inspect the returned object and the function help; pass the same `tool_name` to the plotter when applicable.

## 9 · Malignancy and phenotype association

| Task | Runner | Plotter | Non-negotiable contract |
|---|---|---|---|
| expression-derived CNV | `RunCNV()` | `CNVPlot()` | genome, method/backend, valid normal reference, sample field |
| bulk-phenotype-linked cells | `RunScissor()` | `ScissorPlot()` | aligned bulk features/samples/phenotype and family |

Neither runner establishes clinical malignancy or causality. Require orthogonal validation and preserve the full reference/phenotype design.

### Perturbation and virtual knockout

| Task | Runner | Plotter | Boundary |
|---|---|---|---|
| prioritize responding cell types | `RunAugur()` | stored Augur result / task-appropriate SCOP display | classifier separability, not effect size |
| in-silico gene knockout | `RunscTenifoldKnk()` | `scTenifoldKnkPlot()` | network prediction, not experimental knockout |

Real perturbation studies still need guide assignment, perturbation efficiency, off-target review, independent samples, and an appropriate sample-level model.

## 10 · Spatial transcriptomics

| Task | Runner | SCOP plotter | Essential input | Lesson |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| spot/domain display | — | `SpatialSpotPlot()` | image or declared coordinate columns | [spatial](spatial-case.qmd) |
| spatial variable features | `RunSpatialVariableFeatures()` | `SpatialVariableFeaturePlot()` | normalized assay, coordinates, method | [spatial](spatial-case.qmd) |
| spatial graph | `RunSpatialNetwork()` | `SpatialNetworkPlot()` | image/coordinates, k/radius, graph name | [spatial](spatial-case.qmd) |
| neighbourhoods | `RunSpatialNeighborhood()` | `SpatialNeighborhoodPlot()` | group labels, same graph/coordinate system, tool name | [spatial](spatial-case.qmd) |
| deconvolution | `RunRCTD()` | inspect stored proportions with SCOP spatial plots | compatible single-cell reference, `spacexr` | [spatial](spatial-case.qmd) |
| multi-slice integration | `RunSpatialIntegration()` | `SpatialSpotPlot()` and preservation diagnostics | sample/slice field and method backend | [spatial](spatial-case.qmd) |
| spatial communication | `RunSpatialCellChat()` | `SpatialCellChatPlot()` | group, species, technology, coordinates | [spatial](spatial-case.qmd) |

Spot, domain, deconvolution, and cell-resolved claims are different. Always state which one the function returned.

## 11 · Plotter provenance pattern

```r
plot_record <- list(
  plot_function = "scop::CellDimPlot",
  dataset = "panc8_sub",
  source_checkpoint = "artifacts/checkpoints/cross-source.rds",
  arguments = list(
    group.by = "dataset",
    reduction = "HarmonyUMAP2D",
    show_stat = FALSE
  ),
  allowed_claim = "technical-source mixing diagnostic"
)
```

The graphics device may save or compose the returned SCOP plot. It should not replace the analysis layer with an unrelated manual ggplot while retaining a SCOP caption.

::: {.checkpoint}
**Reference checkpoint**

Before running a new function, verify that it is exported, inspect `args()` and help in the installed version, confirm prerequisites/backends, identify where results are stored, pair it with the correct SCOP plotter, and write the interpretation boundary.
:::

::: {.exercise}
## Practice task

Select one biological question and fill this record: runner, plotter, input checkpoint, assay/layer, grouping/sample fields, backend/reference, expected output location/table, one validation, one failure status, and one sentence the result cannot prove.
:::

For exhaustive per-function argument documentation, use the [upstream SCOP reference index](https://mengxu98.github.io/scop/reference/). This site adds the workflow, evidence, and claim context around those calls.

::: {.boundary}
Function availability proves API presence, not method suitability. A function belongs in an analysis only when its input, design, backend, validation, and claim contract all pass.
:::
